To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nanoscale surface potential fluctuations in Nafon polymer electrolyte films are produced by Brownian hydrogen-ion hopping in the ion-channel network, and can be used to derive local conductivity-relaxations.

the nanoscale fluctuations in low-hydration, thin films of Nafion™ are produced by water-mediated hydrogen-ion hopping in the ion-channel network, and that the fluctuations are non-Gaussian, with a non-trivial dependence on the hydration level of the polymer.

We have developed a new method to probe the nanoscale structure and ion conduction mechanisms of Nafion polymer-electrolyte membranes, using Brownian motion of ions to produce nanoscale fluctuations in surface potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nanoscale ion dynamics in Nafion and its relationship to ion conduction in polymer electrolytes.
the fundamental understanding of ion conduction in Nafion™ polymer electrolytes and the development of a quantitative model for the ion conduction mechanisms.
the nanoscale ion-conduction dynamics of a prototypical polymer electrolyte membrane, and the results are relevant to fuel cells and other applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed fluctuations provide an excellent tool to study ion conduction mechanisms in Nafion and other PEMs.
the observed fluctuations in Nafions are due to the Brownian motion of ions in a network of channels.
the observed fluctuations provide direct evidence that ion hopping occurs on the nanoscale in Nafion™.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ion-channel network is a percolation network, and that the hopping-conductivity model provides a good description of the ion conduction mechanism.

we have shown that the ion conduction network in Nafion is composed of nanometer-sized channels that are connected to each other and that the conduction process in these nanometer-sized channels is governed by ion hopping.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed ion dynamics are dominated by the slowest, lowest-energy ion conduction pathways.
the ion-channel network is highly heterogeneous, with ion hopping rates ranging over several orders of magnitude.

ion conduction in PEM is dominated by hopping of hydrated protons within the ion-channel networks, and that ion-channel network connectivity is a major factor in determining ion conduction properties.
